title: Exact Uniform Sampling of Contingency Tables with Arbitrary Margins
coverage:
Read all sections in full: model and graph, signatures, transport, dense, algorithms. Checks, by section:
(1) Sec. 2: verified the repair map (feasibility, capacity, injectivity with completions, prefix preservation and the special value at s), Lemma small-entry (double counting with labels (i',j',h)), and Prop stationary-success (Λ ≤ (1+d²)Z_0, 4/d⁴ union bound, bijection of successful pairs with Ω).
(2) Sec. 3 laminar lemma: checked the K = 11ᵀ − Σ a_G 1_G1_Gᵀ telescoping and the diagonal handling. Pair-summation lemma: re-derived v^T M_j e_a and v^T M_j e_b, the exact expansion giving (pair-one), and the case analysis at the endpoints and for B=2. Checked the summation by parts with w_j = j(D'−j). Numerically tested Prop 3.4 (at most one positive eigenvalue after balanced summation) on 2806 random softened instances (2–3 × 2–3 grids, capacities 2–3, random context, summed and active roles, η in {0.1,…,0.9}), with 0 violations.
(3) Sec. 4: checked child log-concavity from the 2×2 determinant. Conditional transport: node balance, the potential increment, the mixed-term cancellation and new–new square identity (future monotonicity), the root bound via V_12 ≤ (U+1)²c_t, leaf-clique disjointness, cancelling double representations of defects, and the η→0 limit. Also checked c ≤ max(z−,z+) through the repair, the variance decomposition with disjoint E_σ per level, and the defect extension. Brute-force computed the exact graph Poincaré constant on about 60 tiny instances (U=2,3): constants ≤ 3, far below the bound. The repair always landed on a feasible transversal with f(X) ≤ f(R(X)).
(4) Sec. 6: reversibility of Metropolis-by-completion (c_XY = c_YX), rejection < 1/2 via small-entry with a=L, the inverse-gap arithmetic, the coupling error budget, and the GLMP domination (1−δ)p_k ≤ 1/M with Mδ ≤ 1 and its integer residual weights.
(5) Sec. 5: bin representation, the Lipschitz bound 1/B on coefficients, the interior point, bin acceptance ≥ 1/64, the cut/conductance argument with M = (1−t)S + tD, the mixing lemma (K = 2/κ²), and the offset discretisation error.
Not re-verified line by line: the exact tabulation's bit-length bookkeeping and the Prékopa–Leindler slice-regularity details.
main_claim: Poly-time (in m, n, log N) approximately uniform sampler with 2^-k TV error, and an exactly uniform sampler with polynomial expected bit cost, for nonnegative integer contingency tables with arbitrary binary margins. Route: padded small/large slot decomposition; a Metropolis chain on small states weighted by completion counts, with a Poincaré inequality via a Lorentzian-type signature closed under balanced-pair summation plus a recursive signed flow; dense completions drawn by a bin-chain DKM/Morris-style sampler; then GLMP residual-mixture correction.
sibling_notes: Sibling rank257 (FPRAS for cell-bounded tables) also reported no_gap_found using closely related machinery (laminar log-concave factors, balanced summation, one-hole transport). This paper's signature/transport core is consistent with it. Note this paper claims to resolve a well-known open problem (poly-time sampling for arbitrary margins); despite that, I found no step that fails.
